templates_considered: RET-001 audit_log_protected (soc2, hipaa): fits the audit trail ask. Used as-is with the default audit_log / record_audit_event names.
CONF-010 sensitive_tables_need_login: close to the customer-email tracking, but it requires login and does not require an audit call. Not used directly; CUST-EMAIL-010 borrows its rule shape.
CONF-012 confidential_tables_tagged: would tag the email tables, but it tags by field name and does not audit. Not used.
No template for runaway AI cost or retry loops. Built COST-010 from statement.containment.
No template for retry caps. Dropped (see ask_parts_not_covered).

rules.covers: AI call inside a loop (placeholder statement name)
only the audit function writes the audit log (template)
tables with customer email are tagged
anything reaching email tables requires login and calls the audit function

ask_parts_not_covered.part: a background task kept retrying forever
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists: no check reads task retry settings (object.settings_forbidden lists task active and datasource only)

ask_parts_not_covered.part: last month an AI call inside a loop cost me $900 (dollar spend cap)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists for spend or budgets
couldn't tell how: the catalogue does not list the AI call statement names, so the rule uses a placeholder ai.prompt and may match nothing

ask_parts_not_covered.part: track who changed what on tables holding customer emails
ask_parts_not_covered.why: partly covered: the audit call and login are enforced on each object, but a write done without the audit call through a shared function is only caught if that function is in scope

assumptions: Customer email tables carry an email field and can be tagged pii.
Audit table name audit_log and function record_audit_event (template defaults).
AI call statement name ai.prompt (placeholder, not confirmed).
confusions: Which statement name is the AI call. The catalogue lists outbound kinds (agent.llm) but no AI statement name. The skill says an unknown name is a rule warning, which I confirmed with the parser, but I still had to guess.
Whether a retry limit or spend cap has any check. The catalogue has no retry or cost check, and the skill does not say to use a workaround. I dropped those parts rather than invent a check.
Whether a field-level email requirement belongs in table.tag_required, which only checks a tag is present, not that anything sets it. Unclear how a tag gets applied from policy.

The 'who changed what' part: object.tagged_table_access checks that objects call the audit function, but it does not check that the audit call records the change. The template skips this and the reply says so.
wished_for: The AI call statement names listed in the catalogue or a recipe for AI cost controls.
A check or template for task retry limits (e.g. a setting or statement check on a task's retry value).
A recipe for 'track changes to a table' that combines the audit template with tagged_table_access, since the two checks look similar but do different jobs.
why_confidence: All three files parse (warnings only: names not on this branch and the placeholder ai.prompt). The policies cover the audit trail well but the AI loop check depends on a guessed statement name, and the retry and spend parts have no check at all.
